# Reliability of the roles

<!-- Generated by `cargo run -p codev-evals -- docs` from evals/baseline/report.json and run.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

codev's reviewing roles are measured, not assumed. This page shows how they scored the last time the evaluation suite ran, on the run committed in the repository as its baseline. It is generated from that baseline and changes with it.

## What the suite measures

The suite is a set of small projects, each with a planned change. A **seeded** case hides defects a role should find, each with its severity, its location and its category of issue; a **clean control** hides none. Claude Code runs one skill step on each case with a single role, and the suite scores the review record the role writes: the defects found and missed, the findings that match no defect (**false positives**), whether each quoted evidence is really at the lines it cites, and whether the severity agrees with the expected one. [Measuring the roles](roles.md#measuring-the-roles) gives the rules.

## What it does not measure

It is not a benchmark of models, and not a promise that a role finds every defect of your project. It does not measure how useful a correct finding is to you, nor the roles that write the plan (the analyst, the architect, the tech lead…): only the roles that review. A score describes these cases, on this model, on the day of the run.

## The run

- Date: 2026-10-13
- Model: Claude Code's default
- Claude Code: 2.1.289
- codev: 0.6.1
- Cases: 40 (25 seeded, 15 clean controls)
- Cost: 15.18 USD

## At a glance

<dl class="rel-tiles"><div class="rel-tile"><dt>Recall</dt><dd><span class="rel-tile-value">1.00</span><span class="rel-tile-note">39 of 39 seeded defects found</span></dd></div><div class="rel-tile"><dt>Evidence validity</dt><dd><span class="rel-tile-value">1.00</span><span class="rel-tile-note">139 of 139 quotes found at the cited lines</span></dd></div><div class="rel-tile"><dt>False positives</dt><dd><span class="rel-tile-value">52</span><span class="rel-tile-note">1.3 per case; a role fails above 2</span></dd></div><div class="rel-tile"><dt>Roles within the thresholds</dt><dd><span class="rel-tile-value">1 of 9</span><span class="rel-tile-note"><span class="rel-icon-over" aria-hidden="true">▲</span> 8 fail at least one</span></dd></div></dl>

**The run fails its own thresholds.** 8 of 9 roles report more than 2 false positives: accessibility, migration, newcomer, ops, performance, privacy, security, skeptic. Precision is the roles' weak point: they report plausible issues that the case does not hold. Reducing these false positives without losing what the roles find is the next work planned on the roles. Every seeded defect was found: on this model, recall does not tell the roles apart, and the differences show in false positives and severity agreement.

## The thresholds

A role fails when its recall is under 0.50, when it reports more than 2 false positives, or when less than 0.80 of its checked evidence is valid — the suite's defaults, `--min-recall`, `--max-false-positives` and `--min-evidence`. A role with no seeded case has no recall, and one with no checked finding no evidence validity: neither fails on it.

- <span class="rel-icon-over" aria-hidden="true">▲</span> **accessibility** fails: false positives 4 > 2
- <span class="rel-icon-over" aria-hidden="true">▲</span> **migration** fails: false positives 5 > 2
- <span class="rel-icon-over" aria-hidden="true">▲</span> **newcomer** fails: false positives 6 > 2
- <span class="rel-icon-over" aria-hidden="true">▲</span> **ops** fails: false positives 11 > 2

- <span class="rel-icon-over" aria-hidden="true">▲</span> **skeptic** fails: false positives 9 > 2
- <span class="rel-icon-ok" aria-hidden="true">✓</span> Within every threshold: **tracer**

## The limits

- **One run per case.** A model does not answer the same way twice: each score is one noisy point. A role is compared before and after a change on the same model, not across days or models.
- **Only what the cases cover.** 40 cases, 25 of them seeded with 39 defects. A kind of defect that no case seeds is not measured: a recall of 1.00 means these defects were found, not every defect.
- **A controlled context.** Each case is a small project reviewed by one role alone, within a fixed budget and time. Your project is larger, and the roles review it together.
- **Not a guarantee.** The scores describe the roles on this model and this version of Claude Code. Another model may score differently. Read what the roles report before acting on it.

## Run it yourself

From a clone of the repository, with Claude Code installed and signed in. A run calls a model: this one cost 15.18 USD.

```bash
cargo build --bin codev
cargo run -p codev-evals -- run --out target/evals/mine
cargo run -p codev-evals -- score target/evals/mine
```

The observations, the reports and the run's metadata are in [`evals/baseline`](https://github.com/mairistem/codev/tree/main/evals/baseline). The [contributing guide](https://github.com/mairistem/codev/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#changing-a-role) explains how a change to a role is measured.
